approved_text: There are only finitely many pairs of natural numbers (n, k) with k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2k such that the least prime factor of the binomial coefficient C(n, k) exceeds max(⌊n/k⌋, k).
draft: There are only finitely many pairs of natural numbers (n, k) with k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2k such that the least prime factor of the binomial coefficient C(n, k) exceeds max(⌊n/k⌋, k).
source_docstrings:
For all $n\ge 2k$ the least prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$ is $\le\max(n/k,k)$, with only
finitely many exceptions.
source_lean:
theorem erdos_1094 :
    {(n, k) : ℕ × ℕ | 0 < k ∧ 2 * k ≤ n ∧ (n.choose k).minFac > max (n / k) k}.Finite
